tags.gist: Supports responsible medical AI but wants a clear regulatory line between AI augmenting a physician and AI supplanting physician judgment.
Is especially concerned about systems that diagnose, decide treatment, prescribe or set disposition without meaningful physician oversight.
Says overall accuracy cannot establish safety; rare catastrophic errors such as missed time-sensitive diagnoses mean severity must be weighed.
Wants testing under realistic conditions with atypical, complex and vulnerable patients, since benchmarks and retrospective data cannot reproduce clinical medicine.
Wants safeguards to rise with autonomy: prospective validation for systems initiating treatment or prescribing, and licensed clinician review for high-risk decisions.
Calls post-deployment surveillance essential, monitoring high-risk systems for deterioration, unexpected behavior and adverse outcomes, with significant events reportable.
Says physicians should not automatically be blamed for AI chosen by organizations; developers and institutions should bear responsibility, and override authority must be real.
Warns that financial gains from replacing physicians may push autonomous AI beyond its safety evidence, and lower cost is not evidence of safety.
Says patients deserve to know when AI substantially shapes their care and whether a licensed clinician reviewed consequential decisions.
Sets the objective as physician-led, AI-assisted care rather than replacing accountable professionals because it is technically or economically possible.
Urges FDA to preserve physician oversight of consequential decisions, require real-world validation and surveillance, set accountability and shield patients from premature substitution.
